findings.reason: The protected source is an expert iterative postorder solution. Each node receives one complete validity/bounds/size/best summary, empty-child sentinels make strict joins uniform, and the explicit expanded flag avoids recursion-depth risk. The local TreeNode model and naming are clear, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 333 and its Python largestBSTSubtree surface. The Reference preserves strict global BST ordering, complete rooted-subtree semantics, both source examples, both constraints, the note, the linear-time follow-up, and the source tree visual.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064425670. Its expanded-postorder traversal, empty summary, strict boundary test, valid and invalid summary construction, and root result structurally align with the protected app-local solve body; only the local model and native class wrapper differ.

The legal 32, 64, and 128-node left-skewed BST tiers span 4x and make every rooted subtree valid. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.02 relative growth and 1.02x; correct validation and counting from every root passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +0.97 and 14.20x.
The Approach exactly defines each child summary, strict joining condition, invalid-subtree propagation, iterative postorder schedule, induction argument, and O(n) time and space.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples and explanation status, both constraints, the note and follow-up sections, and an independent diagram corresponding to the source visual.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first, in source order, with their exact level-order trees and outputs; the previously substituted complete-BST and singleton rows were reclassified as authored coverage rather than source samples.
The empty-tree and single-node trials cover the minimum node counts; a 10,000-node left chain was verified outside cases.json, and the visible value-extremes trial uses both -10,000 and 10,000.
Duplicate children and an all-duplicate tree enforce strict rather than non-strict BST ordering, including the singleton fallback when no multi-node subtree is valid.
A deep value in the right subtree that lies below the root proves that immediate-child checks are insufficient, while the complete-subtree trial prevents omitting a violating descendant.
Balanced, left-skewed, signed, whole-tree, and descendant-only optima exercise empty, singleton, partial-tree, and entire-tree return modes.

An independent inorder-and-count oracle verified all 11 authored results and the target matched it on 107,725 exhaustive ordered binary trees through six nodes using labels {-1, 0, 1}; the iterative target also returned 10,000 on a legal maximum-depth left chain.
All 11 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 32-, 64-, and 128-node left-skewed workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
